rows.focus: Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk of malnutrition, feeding difficulties and altered body composition beyond infancy. Excessive serotonergic activity can stimulate hypothalamic pathways regulating arginine vasopressin secretion, resulting in euvolemic hyponatremia and hyponatremic encephalopathy while simultaneously producing the characteristic neuromuscular, autonomic, and mental status abnormalities of SS. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent mobile cognitive behavioral intervention package for fatigue management among patients with IBD in remission and to explore factors associated with engagement with the intervention and its effectiveness. This was an open-label, waitlist-controlled randomized controlled trial. Given these roles, magnesium supplementation has received increasing attention as a potential strategy to support exercise performance and recovery. This review aimed to evaluate the current evidence regarding magnesium intake and its effects on exercise performance, skeletal muscle recovery, body composition, and inflammatory responses. A focused narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed to identify studies published between 2000 and 2025 that contained the terms "magnesium" and "muscle" in the title. In youth sport, pain is often normalized or viewed primarily through an injury-centered lens, despite its potential to shape function, participation patterns, and athletic trajectories over time. This focused narrative review aimed to (1) synthesize current evidence on persistent and recurrent musculoskeletal pain in young athletes and (2) propose a developmentally informed biopsychosocial framework for understanding its implications for RTS. Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, and SPORTDiscus for studies published from 1 January 2006, through 28 February 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking and targeted hand-searching of reference lists. rows.title: Exploring the Effect of Nutrition on Fetal Development in Pregnant Patients With Inflammatory Gut Diseases: A Scoping Review.
rows.focus: Inflammatory gut diseases (IGDs) are increasing in prevalence and pose unique challenges during pregnancy. Nutritional deficiencies, particularly in magnesium, folate, and vitamin B12, exacerbate these risks due to both inadequate intake and malabsorption. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the role of nutrition in fetal development among pregnant women with IGDs, highlighting dietary strategies that may enhance maternal gastrointestinal health and optimize fetal outcomes. This study was designed as a scoping review to examine the relationship between IGDs, pregnancy, and nutrition. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a search was conducted for peer-reviewed literature using the databases Embase, Web of Science, Ovid MEDLINE, and CINAHL. rows.title: Precision cognitive neurorehabilitation: dose, adaptivity, digital therapeutics and implementation.
rows.focus: Cognitive deficits are determinants of long-term disability and socio-professional reintegration across neurological disorders, including stroke, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, and neurodegenerative diseases. Despite evidence supporting cognitive neurorehabilitation, its implementation remains heterogeneous, and therapeutic parameters are insufficiently defined. The authors reviewed the published literature from PubMed and Google Scholar from 1 January 2015 to 30 June 2026, supplemented by seminal publications. Clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational and proof-of-concept studies were prioritized. This brief narrative review examines restorative and compensatory cognitive neurorehabilitation for deficits of attention, executive functions, language and disorders of consciousness in people after stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), older adults, and those with neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, including multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. rows.title: An audit of the fracture liaison service at Helen Joseph Tertiary Hospital, Johannesburg, South Africa.
rows.focus: Fragility fractures are increasing worldwide, yet osteoporosis often remains underdiagnosed and untreated. This study found a high burden of osteoporosis risk factors among patients enrolled in a South African fracture liaison service, highlighting the need for structured secondary prevention. These findings support expansion of fracture liaison services to improve long-term patient outcomes in resource-limited settings. Fragility fractures (FF) driven by osteoporosis result in high morbidity and mortality and are a global health concern. Fracture liaison services (FLSs) are the gold standard for secondary prevention, yet data on their implementation and patient profiles in South Africa remain sparse. Health information technology (HIT) adoption has emerged as a promising structural solution for improving the quality of clinical processes and patient outcomes at hospitals. rows.title: A Short-Term Longitudinal Study on Arm/Shoulder Functions Following Breast Cancer Surgery and Its Implications on Shoulder Physiotherapy.
rows.focus: Enhanced survival following breast cancer diagnosis has brought into focus various long term sequelae of treatment, one of the most common of which are arm/shoulder problems (ASPs). rows.title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects diabetes-associated cognitive decline by enhancing leucine catabolism and suppressing neuronal excessive mitophagy.
rows.focus: Dysregulation of the gut-brain metabolic axis has been implicated in the progression of diabetes-associated cognitive decline (DACD), yet its underlying mechanism remains largely unknown. Our results revealed that AKK bacteria hold the capacity to catabolize leucine, and the elevated leucine levels observed in diabetic mice and patients are partly attributed to a low abundance of AKK bacteria. Mechanistically, leucine directly modulated the phosphorylation of TBK1 and, in turn, phosphorylated the autophagy adaptor OPTN, thereby enhancing its binding capacity to LC3 and Ub chains and triggering neuronal excessive mitophagy. Therefore, this study uncovers a new mechanism of the gut-brain metabolic axis involved in DACD progression and provides a novel perspective for gut-targeted therapy of cognitive disorders.

rows.title: 16S rRNA Datasets of Gut Microbiota in Stent-Based Diverting Technique and Ileostomy from A Prospective, Open-Label, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
rows.focus: Accumulating evidence implicates gut dysbiosis in postoperative complications and delayed intestinal recovery after rectal cancer surgery. rows.title: Impact of a Mediterranean diet and physical activity intervention on the gut microbiome and faecal metabolites: findings from the MedEx-UK randomised controlled trial.
rows.focus: Diet and physical activity (PA) are potential modulators of the gut microbiome, although research findings are inconsistent, and few studies have explored their combined effects. rows.title: Intestinal-Bone Axis Mediated by Bifidobacterium: Mechanistic Analysis and Therapeutic Potential in Osteoporosis.
rows.focus: Osteoporosis is one of the most prevalent metabolic bone diseases worldwide, and current pharmacological options are limited by adverse effects and are poorly suited to long-term use, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic targets. rows.title: Weight Gain During SSRI Therapy: The Potential Role of the Gut Microbiota-A Narrative Review and Mechanistic Hypothesis.
rows.focus: Introduction: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) remain the first-line pharmacological treatment for depressive disorders. rows.title: Comparative Effects of Microbiota-Modifying Interventions for Gastrointestinal Disorders in Adults with Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
rows.focus: Chemotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) frequently causes gastrointestinal (GI) toxicities, which may affect treatment adherence and quality of life. rows.title: Coffee, the Gut Microbiome, and Host Metabolism: Gastrointestinal Fate, Microbial Transformation, Mechanistic Insights, and Prospects for Precision Nutrition.
rows.focus: Coffee is one of the most widely consumed beverages worldwide and a major dietary source of bioactive compounds, including caffeine, chlorogenic acids (CGAs), trigonelline, non-digestible polysaccharides, and roasting-derived melanoidins. rows.title: Targeting the Gut-Bone Axis with Prebiotics, Probiotics, Synbiotics, and Postbiotics: From Mechanistic Plausibility to Clinical Bone Outcomes.
rows.focus: Osteoporosis is a major skeletal disorder. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived mechanisms may contribute to bone remodeling. The evidence was evaluated according to intervention type and outcome. We focused on bone turnover markers, bone mineral density, and the duration of exposure required for these outcomes to become clinically meaningful. Recent randomized trials and meta-analyses were also compared in a semi-quantitative synthesis to show where findings are consistent and where they remain conflicting.

rows.title: Vaginal Ecosystem During Gestation and Puerperium: Microbiota, Dysbiosis, Infection and Fetal-Maternal Implications.

rows.title: Microbiome signatures and mechanistic pathways in pediatric obesity: from early-life risk to precision interventions.
rows.focus: The gut microbiota is increasingly recognized as a modulator of metabolic health in children, influencing nutrient absorption, immune tone, epithelial barrier function, and energy homeostasis. rows.title: Gut microbiota and systemic sclerosis: Mechanistic insights and microbial therapies.
rows.focus: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease characterized by progressive fibrosis in the skin and multiple organs. The cause and mechanism of SSc remain largely elusive, and there are limited therapeutic options available that effectively alter the progression of fibrosis associated with the disease. In this review, we provide a comprehensive summary of clinical evidence regarding gut microbiota dysbiosis in SSc, examines the potential mechanisms of gut microbiota involvement in SSc pathogenesis, and discusses recent advancements in diagnostic and therapeutic approaches based on gut microbiota for SSc. Finally, we emphasize the current limitations as well as future research directions. We aim to comprehensively present the current status of research on the relationship between gut microbiota and SSc, thereby offering valuable insights for further exploration of the pathogenesis of the disease and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies based on the gut microbiota and its metabolites.

rows.title: Importance of faecal sample collection in prospective cohort studies to evaluate the effect of the gut microbiome on cancer development.
rows.focus: The gut microbiome has been linked to cancer in many cross-sectional studies. These studies compared individuals with and without cancer, but they do not establish causation. rows.focus: The pediatric gut microbiome influences immune maturation, neurodevelopment, and disease susceptibility. Probiotic supplementation has been investigated across multiple childhood conditions, yet strain-specific efficacy remains inconsistent. rows.title: The interplay between vitamin D3 and Nrf2 signaling: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potentials.

rows.focus: Post-acidification during storage limits the use of multiple probiotics in fermented dairy products.
